title: Pick the Best: Formal Charge Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Aarav draws carbon dioxide two ways, and both have full octets. Which one is right? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 4, Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure) we answer with one simple count: formal charge.

You will see the idea with pocket money (coins of your own count fully, coins in a shared jar count half), build the formula FC = V - L - 1/2 B step by step on the oxygen of water, and work out the formal charges of ozone on the molecule bench (+1, 0 and -1). We compare a real charge with a formal charge, pick the better CO2 structure, and check that formal charges add up to the charge of the ammonium ion. Then the exam trap, an original JEE and NEET pattern question on the nitrate ion with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 41 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:
0:00 Bills, pizza and pocket money
0:30 Counting coins: the idea
0:54 The formula step by step
1:18 Ozone on the molecule bench
2:04 Pause and think: a real charge?
2:18 Smallest formal charges win
2:23 Worked example: two CO2 structures
3:01 Charges add up: ammonium ion
3:23 Exam trap and where it is asked
3:42 Practice question (JEE and NEET pattern)
4:23 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Limitations of the Octet Rule. Some atoms are happy with fewer than eight electrons, and some hold more.
